question.text: A bond has a modified duration of 5.2. If the yield rises by 0.25% (25 bps), the approximate price change is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The duration-based approximation is percent price change is approximately equal to negative modified duration multiplied by the decimal change in yield: -5.2 x 0.0025 = -0.013, i.e. approximately -1.3%. The Trap: +1.3% reverses the sign: when yields rise, bond prices fall. -5.2% applies the full modified duration without scaling by the 25 bps move. +5.2% reverses both the sign and the scaling. Note: Always convert basis points to decimals before applying the duration formula: 25 bps = 0.0025, not 0.25. Sign matters too — rising yields produce a negative price change.
